label: History
value: Adrian Treleaven traveled to Seven Gulls.
unit: Adrian Treleaven traveled to Seven Gulls for a three-month break to recover his strength and seek inspiration for a major Canadian novel. Upon arriving, he was driven by Miss Winifred to Nell Carrow's home, where he was introduced to Lorna Vane, his prospective landlady, and was immediately struck by her extraordinary beauty. Recognizing his literary talent and maternal connection to the area, Nell introduced him to Captain Saul. Adrian proposed writing Captain Saul's "life-book," weaving the captain's maritime adventures together with the romantic thread of his lost love, Margaret.

label: History
value: Over the summer, Adrian set up a workroom in the lighthouse next to Captain Saul's room.
unit: Over the summer, Adrian set up a workroom in the lighthouse next to Captain Saul's room, throwing himself passionately into writing the book while relying on the captain's knowledge of local seafaring lore. In his afternoons and evenings, he joined Nell, Hugh Carrow, Captain Saul, and Lorna on shore excursions, clambakes, fishing trips, and fireside gatherings. During his stay, Adrian fell deeply in love with Lorna Vane. In late August, in the flower-filled garden of the ancient dwelling, he confessed his love to Lorna, and they pledged their devotion to one another. Before departing, he attended a final gathering by the driftwood fire where Captain Saul bestowed a blessing upon him, Lorna, and their friends.

value: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby resides in Sowerby's Hollow near Brierley
unit: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby resides in Sowerby's Hollow near Brierley with her husband, Thomas. She watched Obed Abernethy bring the orphan Nell into the neighborhood and later observed Thirza Abernethy taking in the twins, Robin and Lucy Farrow. When meeting young Nell at Thirza's home, Mrs. Sowerby bluntly criticized the girl's thin frame, freckles, and red hair, provoking a passionate outburst from Nell. Despite Mr. Pettifer's complaints about her persistent fundraising for a vestry room carpet and her blunt style of speaking, Nell came to appreciate Mrs. Sowerby's underlying generosity, such as her forgiveness when Timothy Cotton took butter from her dairy. As her husband Thomas's health fluctuated, she spent much of her time caring for him, though she took advantage of his periods of improvement to take trips into town, visit neighbors like the newly returned Mrs. Pettifer, and continue participating in local community life.

label: History
value: Ambrose swore publicly during a general election campaign fifteen years prior.
unit: During a fiercely contested general election campaign fifteen years prior, Ambrose swore publicly that he would refrain from shaving his face or trimming his hair until his political party, the Grits, returned to power. Because the Liberals failed to achieve victory, he maintained his promise into middle age, growing out his hair and beard and earning a reputation for looking like an oddity. Throughout his life, he remained acquainted with Captain Saul, with whom he went cod-fishing. Eventually, he became engaged to Miss Winifred, agreeing to let her wear a wedding veil if she wished, and married her about four weeks after their arrangement.

label: History
value: Anthony attended Brierley School.
unit: Anthony attended Brierley School under the instruction of Nell Harcourt, sitting at a corner desk by himself. On the first day of class, he displayed clear hostility toward Nell and poured water from his slate bottle onto Aurelia Clay's neck. Kept inside during recess, he listened to Nell's lecture on gentlemanly behavior completely unaffected. Later, when Nell lost her temper, she punished him with a pointer, causing him to cry and step back. Rather than holding a grudge, the whipping earned his respect, as he considered the punishment to be as effective as a man's. Afterwards, he broke his habit of ignoring Nell by offering to carry her books through the snow on her way to school.

label: History
value: Aunt Euphemia was left alone in a large house after her only daughter married and left for the mission field.
unit: After her only daughter married and left for the mission field, Aunt Euphemia was left alone in a large house until Mabel Colby invited her to relocate to Portmaris/Wexcombe to keep house for Mabel, Nell, Honora, and Cressy at Tabby's Place. Upon moving in, she brought along her two cats, the Sarah-cat and Joseph. During the Christmas break, she chose to stay behind at Tabby's Place to care for the cats and keep the house warm rather than leave them alone. Throughout their years at college, she provided a warm, welcoming presence for the girls and their visiting friends, while gently offering her perspectives on young suitors and life.

label: History
value: Barney harbored a vast admiration for Nell Harcourt.
unit: Barney harbored a vast admiration for Nell Harcourt and felt immense pride driving her to a concert at Pale Sands in his buggy. Because he lacked conversation skills, Nell spent much of the ride chatting behind her back to the other girls, while Barney smirked and chuckled quietly. Later, after his father deeded him the upper farm in his own name, Barney sought to take Nell as his wife. Due to his extreme bashfulness, he repeatedly harassed his sister Odette until she agreed to propose to Nell on his behalf. Barney offered to wait until Nell finished her college education if necessary, though he preferred a spring wedding before planting; however, Nell firmly rejected the proposal, as she had never considered him in that way.

label: History
value: Leonora Bowman was born.
unit: Born as Leonora Bowman, she went to live with Miss Rosalind Penrose at Echo Cottage in exchange for room, board, and clothes, succeeding her older sisters Belinda (Belinda the First), Julietta (Belinda the Second), and Evelina (Belinda the Third). Because of her sisters' resemblance, Miss Rosalind called her 'Belinda the Fourth' to avoid confusion. Unlike her elder sisters, Belinda never mocked Miss Rosalind's imaginative pretending and served as her dedicated helper, despite her tendency to let tea boil or accidentally shatter dishes. During a visit by Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke, Belinda assisted with serving tea and demonstrated the estate's famous echoes by sounding a tin horn and chuckling for the visitors. As she approached her teenage years, she privately attempted to practice walking and speaking like Nell, whom she idolized. Recognizing signs of illness and loneliness in Miss Rosalind after a winter walk, Belinda confided her deep worries to Nell. Later, when Stephen Stanhope's visit was arranged, she confronted Nell to learn the secret and voiced her earnest hope that Stephen would marry Miss Rosalind so her mistress would be looked after when Belinda reached sixteen and had to move to Boston.

unit: Born as Leonora Bowman, she went to live with Miss Rosalind Penrose at Echo Cottage in exchange for room, board, and clothes, succeeding her older sisters Belinda (Belinda the First), Julietta (Belinda the Second), and Evelina (Belinda the Third). Because of her sisters' resemblance, Miss Rosalind called her 'Belinda the Fourth' to avoid confusion. Unlike her elder sisters, Belinda never mocked Miss Rosalind's imaginative pretending and served as her dedicated helper, despite her tendency to let tea boil or accidentally shatter dishes. During a visit by Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke, Belinda assisted with serving tea and demonstrated the estate's famous echoes by sounding a tin horn and chuckling for the visitors. As she approached her teenage years, she privately attempted to practice walking and speaking like Nell, whom she idolized. Recognizing signs of illness and loneliness in Miss Rosalind after a winter walk, Belinda confided her deep worries to Nell. Later, when Stephen Stanhope's visit was arranged, she confronted Nell to learn the secret and voiced her earnest hope that Stephen would marry Miss Rosalind so her mistress would be looked after when Belinda reached sixteen and had to move to Boston.

label: History
value: Captain Saul served as a mariner for decades.
unit: Captain Saul served for decades as a mariner before settling at the Seven Gulls light as keeper. Upon the arrival of Dr. Hugh Carrow and his wife Nell, he welcomed them to Seven Gulls, bringing them fresh trout and quickly forming a close friendship with both. He regularly entertained them with recounting accounts of his seafaring days and showed Nell his handwritten life-book, which recorded his ocean voyages for his nephew Joe. When author Adrian Treleaven visited, Nell introduced him to Captain Saul and his logbook. Inspired by the old captain's extensive experiences, Treleaven utilized material from Captain Saul's life-book to author a successful biographical work titled The Life Book. Captain Saul later passed away in Seven Gulls.

Upon the arrival of Dr. Hugh Carrow and his wife Nell, he welcomed them to Seven Gulls, bringing them fresh trout and quickly forming a close friendship with both. He regularly entertained them with recounting accounts of his seafaring days and showed Nell his handwritten life-book, which recorded his ocean voyages for his nephew Joe. When author Adrian Treleaven visited, Nell introduced him to Captain Saul and his logbook. Inspired by the old captain's extensive experiences, Treleaven utilized material from Captain Saul's life-book to author a successful biographical work titled The Life Book. Captain Saul later passed away in Seven Gulls.

value: Cedric is imaginative.

He holds high ethical standards, refusing to associate with those who use coarse language. While typical boys dislike affection, he will warmly offer kisses to those who remind him of his mother's loving gaze.

label: History
value: Cedric moved from Boston
unit: Cedric moved from Boston to reside with his grandmother, Mrs. Stanhope, along the shore road in Brierley. At school, he became a beloved student of Nell Harcourt, excelling at games and earning the respect of his peers after engaging in a fight with St. Clair Trask over a patriotic debate. Having few real local companions by the beach, Cedric invented elaborate imaginary stone figures and adventures by the sea. Nell introduced him to Miss Rosalind Penrose at the stone house, where his resemblance to his father and his polite, endearing demeanor earned him Miss Rosalind's deep affection and friendship.

label: History
value: At seventeen, Clementine was engaged to Martin Crawford.
unit: At seventeen, Clementine was engaged to Martin Crawford, but he tragically drowned at sea, leaving her forever changed. She lived for many years with her sister Harriet in a remote house on a hill, mostly staying home and attending the Episcopal church in Kettlebridge. She agreed to give music lessons to Nell Harcourt's charges simply because it pleased her. One evening near a spring, she met the widowed minister John Ashdown, who crafted a birch-bark cup for her to drink from; she cherished the cup as a keepsake. Over the autumn, Mr. Ashdown courted her, though rumors later spread that she rejected him out of fear of being a stepmother to his wild children. When young Ida Ashdown came to her begging her to marry their father for his happiness, Clementine reassured Ida of her love for them and sent a note to Mr. Ashdown agreeing to marry him.

value: Edmund grew up at Hollowmere.
unit: Edmund grew up at Hollowmere alongside his siblings, spending much of his time reading poetry, enjoying nature in places like Fern Hollow, and quietly writing an epic poem modeled after Marmion. Due to his solitary nature and avoidance of fights, he was viewed as mild by his schoolmates at Glen St. Agnes. One evening, after Dan Coyle insulted his mother's writings and Grace Ashdown, Edmund confronted Coyle in a physical fight despite his internal fear and lack of experience. He emerged victorious, forcing Dan to take back his words. Following the fight, he met Mr. Ashdown, who praised his defense of honor, and returned home to be tended to by his mother.

label: History
value: Flossie attended Brierley School.
unit: Flossie attended Brierley School under Miss Thorne, participating in school recitations despite her open disdain for them. Along with Nell Harcourt, Odette Pullen, and Opal Pettigrew, she took the entrance exams for Regent's Academy in town. She passed the examinations by a thin margin. While attending college, she noted that she pursued higher education solely for learning's sake since she would not need to earn a livelihood. Later, Flossie and her family hosted a send-off celebration for Nell and Hugh Carrow organized by the B.V.I.S., where she acted patronizingly toward Nell.

label: History
value: Grace spent a Saturday morning.
unit: Grace spent a Saturday morning exploring with her siblings, Tobias, Ida, and Rupert. In Mr. Taylor's old barn, they discovered Mary Stubbs hiding in the hayloft and starving. Distressed by Mary's plight, Grace immediately embraced her and ordered Tobias to stop troubling the girl. Following a widely spread story about her rooster Adam, Grace was mocked by her peers at school. Seeking comfort, she went to Fern Hollow to visit Mrs. Carrow. Learning Mrs. Carrow was away, Grace encountered Clementine Ainslie. Encouraged by Miss Ainslie's sincere demeanor, Grace confided the whole story of Adam's fate to her. Concerned that her father might be forced to leave the Glen due to unpaid church wages, Grace took it upon herself to visit Lionel Fairlie. En route, she was accompanied by Edmund Carrow until they encountered Dan Coyle, who insulted her by calling her a pig-girl.

unit: Grace spent a Saturday morning exploring with her siblings, Tobias, Ida, and Rupert. In Mr. Taylor's old barn, they discovered Mary Stubbs hiding in the hayloft and starving. Distressed by Mary's plight, Grace immediately embraced her and ordered Tobias to stop troubling the girl. Following a widely spread story about her rooster Adam, Grace was mocked by her peers at school. Seeking comfort, she went to Fern Hollow to visit Mrs. Carrow. Learning Mrs. Carrow was away, Grace encountered Clementine Ainslie. Encouraged by Miss Ainslie's sincere demeanor, Grace confided the whole story of Adam's fate to her. Concerned that her father might be forced to leave the Glen due to unpaid church wages, Grace took it upon herself to visit Lionel Fairlie. En route, she was accompanied by Edmund Carrow until they encountered Dan Coyle, who insulted her by calling her a pig-girl.

label: History
value: Harriet lived in a remote house on the hill in Fern Hollow.
unit: Harriet lived in a remote house on the hill in Fern Hollow alongside her younger sister, Clementine. Over the years, she tended to dominate and protect Clementine, keeping a quiet domestic life while retaining her wealth and social standing. When the minister Rev. John Knox Ashdown courted Clementine, Harriet was almost always present during his evening visits, engaging him in intellectual conversations about politics and world events. Later, Harriet attended the silver wedding anniversary of the Pollocks, where she encountered Lionel Fairlie for the first time in social settings after many years. She engaged Lionel in a lively debate and soundly defeated him. Returning home at midnight in the moonlight, she discovered Clementine pacing inside the living room waiting to talk to her.

Over the years, she tended to dominate and protect Clementine, keeping a quiet domestic life while retaining her wealth and social standing. When the minister Rev. John Knox Ashdown courted Clementine, Harriet was almost always present during his evening visits, engaging him in intellectual conversations about politics and world events. Later, Harriet attended the silver wedding anniversary of the Pollocks, where she encountered Lionel Fairlie for the first time in social settings after many years. She engaged Lionel in a lively debate and soundly defeated him. Returning home at midnight in the moonlight, she discovered Clementine pacing inside the living room waiting to talk to her.

label: History
value: Ida resides at the old manse
unit: Ida resides at the old manse with her father, Rev. John Knox Ashdown, and her siblings Tobias, Grace, and Rupert. Unlike her siblings, she experiences secret shame over her lack of practical household skills such as cooking and sewing. One Saturday, while exploring Mr. Taylor's pasture barn with her siblings, she nervously accompanied them up to the hayloft, where they discovered the hungry waif Mary Stubbs. Later, Mrs. Hector Twiss attempted to adopt Ida to spite her own family and raise her with wealth and lessons, but her father fiercely rejected the offer out of deep love for Ida and memory of his late wife.

label: History
value: Isolde Pembroke grew up at Pear Hill.
unit: Isolde Pembroke grew up at Pear Hill overlooking Pembroke's pond. During her school days at Brierley, she formed a deep, emotional friendship with Nell Harcourt. After participating in a prank that inadvertently frightened a visiting guest, Miss Pembroke, she stood by in apprehension while Nell helped resolve the tension. Following the visit, Miss Pembroke gifted Isolde a silver bangle bracelet. While Nell went on to join the Regent's class to pursue teaching, Isolde's parents did not plan to send her, causing her path to temporarily diverge from Nell's, though they remained close. She frequently shared gossip, comforted Nell about her freckles, helped with preparations for guests, and remained a faithful confidante when Nell harbored ambitions of writing fiction.

label: History
value: John Ashdown serves as the Presbyterian minister
unit: John Ashdown serves as the Presbyterian minister at Glen St. Agnes. Following the unexpected death of his beloved wife Cecilia, he was left to raise their children—including Tobias, Grace, Ida, Rupert, and Gerald—while managing his pastoral duties. During a walk through Fern Hollow to take a drink from a hidden spring, he engaged in a heart-to-heart conversation with young Edmund Carrow, forming a close friendship with the boy. Shortly after, he encountered Clementine Ainslie by the spring in the moonlight, seeing her clearly for the first time and finding comfort in her presence during subsequent visits. When the wealthy Mrs. Hector Twiss abruptly demanded to adopt his daughter Ida, John grew fiercely defensive and refused to part with his late wife's child. Later, when his son Rupert fell critically ill with double pneumonia after a night spent in the cemetery, John kept a night-long vigil and called for Dr. Carrow's aid until the boy safely recovered. Over the winter, realizing his deep affection for Clementine, he set out through Fern Hollow intending to express his feelings to her.

label: History
value: Lionel Fairlie spent two years courting Harriet Ainslie.
unit: In his youth, Lionel Fairlie spent two years courting Harriet Ainslie, but after a foolish disagreement, he impulsively married Dinah Coyle in a fit of temper. He held contempt for Dinah's weak-willed docility and crushed what little resolve she had, though she bore her submissive life without public complaint until her death ten years later. After feeling cheated over a cow deal by a church session member, Lionel ceased attending church for twenty years, insisting his late wife contribute no more than a single penny during her visits. Following a visit from young Grace Ashdown, he resumed church attendance on the first Sunday of November, making a public stir by teasing Mr. Ashdown about his deceased wife's health and commending his sermon. Entranced upon seeing Harriet Ainslie at church after two decades, he openly resumed his courtship of her. He later pursued Clementine Ainslie to Fern Hollow to obtain her consent to release Harriet from a personal vow, successfully clearing the path for his upcoming marriage.

value: Kit is the eldest son of his family.

label: History
value: Lorna grew up on the old Ainslie farm.
unit: Lorna grew up on the old Ainslie farm. After her father passed away, she inherited money from her grandmother West, enabling her to study at Regent's Academy, where she completed a two-year teaching program in one year and took a job at the Glen schoolhouse. When Abner and Rufus Vane threatened to foreclose on her family's farm, Lorna sacrificed her ambitions and agreed to marry Rufus Vane to spare her mother heartbreak. Following her mother's death and Rufus's departure on a voyage aboard the Four Sisters, she was left to manage the farm alone. Years later, Captain Saul brought back an incapacitated man missing his memory, whom Lorna believed to be Rufus. For eleven years, Lorna devoted herself to his constant care while leasing her farm and accommodating summer boarders like Adrian Treleaven to make ends meet. She developed a close friendship with Nell and Miss Winifred. It was eventually discovered that the man she had nursed for over a decade was actually Rufus's cousin, Laurence Vane, freeing her from her long burden.

When Abner and Rufus Vane threatened to foreclose on her family's farm, Lorna sacrificed her ambitions and agreed to marry Rufus Vane to spare her mother heartbreak. Following her mother's death and Rufus's departure on a voyage aboard the Four Sisters, she was left to manage the farm alone. Years later, Captain Saul brought back an incapacitated man missing his memory, whom Lorna believed to be Rufus. For eleven years, Lorna devoted herself to his constant care while leasing her farm and accommodating summer boarders like Adrian Treleaven to make ends meet. She developed a close friendship with Nell and Miss Winifred. It was eventually discovered that the man she had nursed for over a decade was actually Rufus's cousin, Laurence Vane, freeing her from her long burden.

label: History
value: Lucy was brought to live at Grey Shutters.
unit: Lucy was brought to live at Grey Shutters alongside her twin brother, Robin, under the care of Nell Harcourt and Thirza Abernethy. Before starting school, she agreed at Sunday School to sit with Lily Mott, though she was provisionally placed next to Mirabel Cotton on her first day. At school, Mirabel frightened Lucy with detailed stories of her deceased family members and a ghost uncle, leaving Lucy terrified to go upstairs in the dark alone at night until Nell comforted her. Nell later promised to take Lucy and Robin on a boat ride to the dunes for a shore picnic.

label: History
value: Mabel Colby studied at Regent's Academy.
unit: Mabel Colby studied at Regent's Academy, where she was considered the most beautiful girl in the Second Year classes and formed a close circle of friends with Nell Harcourt and Honora Hollis. Following her third year at Regent's, she worked as a country schoolteacher for two years, managing a wide range of grade levels and dealing with demanding parents. Tired of rural teaching and the fatigue of boarding, Mabel decided to pursue a degree at Wexcombe College by joining the Sophomore class. She proposed a co-living arrangement to Nell and Honora, suggesting they rent and keep house together in Portmaris with her Aunt Euphemia acting as housekeeper. Later, she lived in Portmaris alongside her friends, dealing with domestic antics such as their resident cats, Smudge, Joseph, and the Sarah-cat.

label: History
value: Nell was born in Harborough, Nova Scotia.
unit: Nell was born in a small yellow house in Harborough, Nova Scotia. After losing both of her parents to fever during infancy, she was cared for by guardians and spent time in an asylum until she was eleven years old. She was taken in by Thirza and Obed Abernethy of Grey Shutters in Brierley, avoiding being sent to live with Mrs. Scobie. Upon arriving in Brierley, she formed a lifelong friendship with Isolde Pembroke, swearing a mutual vow of friendship in the Pembrokes' garden. In her youth, Nell attempted to dye her red hair, which disastrously turned green, and made various attempts to erase her freckles. She trained as a schoolteacher at Regent's and later accepted a position as a rural schoolma'am at Coombe Road, staying with Thora Sweet at Wayside. She actively advocated for local community enhancements, co-founding the Brierley Village Improvement Society alongside Hugh Carrow. In adulthood, she married Dr. Hugh Carrow and moved to Seven Gulls.

unit: Nell was born in a small yellow house in Harborough, Nova Scotia. After losing both of her parents to fever during infancy, she was cared for by guardians and spent time in an asylum until she was eleven years old. She was taken in by Thirza and Obed Abernethy of Grey Shutters in Brierley, avoiding being sent to live with Mrs. Scobie. Upon arriving in Brierley, she formed a lifelong friendship with Isolde Pembroke, swearing a mutual vow of friendship in the Pembrokes' garden. In her youth, Nell attempted to dye her red hair, which disastrously turned green, and made various attempts to erase her freckles. She trained as a schoolteacher at Regent's and later accepted a position as a rural schoolma'am at Coombe Road, staying with Thora Sweet at Wayside. She actively advocated for local community enhancements, co-founding the Brierley Village Improvement Society alongside Hugh Carrow. In adulthood, she married Dr. Hugh Carrow and moved to Seven Gulls.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy traveled eight miles on his sorrel mare.
unit: Obed Abernethy traveled eight miles on his sorrel mare to Alder River to collect an orphan boy he and his sister Thirza had arranged to take in from Nova Scotia. Upon arrival, he learned that the train had left behind an eleven-year-old girl, Nell Harcourt, instead of a boy. Unable to inform the child of the mistake on the spot, he brought her back to Grey Shutters. Although Thirza initially reacted with astonishment and disappointment, Obed felt compassion for Nell and supported keeping her. Later, during a winter evening, Obed observed Nell among her peers and realized her wardrobe was noticeably plain compared to theirs. Wanting her to have a modern, attractive dress for Christmas, he ventured to Delford to buy fabric. Distracted by a fashionable female clerk in Samuel Lawson's shop, he flusteredly purchased an unwanted garden rake and brown sugar before consulting Mrs. Sowerby to choose and make a stylish gown for Nell.

unit: Obed Abernethy traveled eight miles on his sorrel mare to Alder River to collect an orphan boy he and his sister Thirza had arranged to take in from Nova Scotia. Upon arrival, he learned that the train had left behind an eleven-year-old girl, Nell Harcourt, instead of a boy. Unable to inform the child of the mistake on the spot, he brought her back to Grey Shutters. Although Thirza initially reacted with astonishment and disappointment, Obed felt compassion for Nell and supported keeping her. Later, during a winter evening, Obed observed Nell among her peers and realized her wardrobe was noticeably plain compared to theirs. Wanting her to have a modern, attractive dress for Christmas, he ventured to Delford to buy fabric. Distracted by a fashionable female clerk in Samuel Lawson's shop, he flusteredly purchased an unwanted garden rake and brown sugar before consulting Mrs. Sowerby to choose and make a stylish gown for Nell.

label: Personality
value: Odette has a relaxed temperament.
unit: Odette has a relaxed, pragmatic, and mild-mannered temperament. Unbothered by grand ideals of inspiration, her primary focus as a teacher was to merit her pay, satisfy the board, and maintain order—favoring firm punishment when necessary. Though not considered particularly clever, she possesses a gentle, uncorrupted, and thoughtful nature that avoids speaking words that might hurt others' feelings.

label: History
value: Odette grew up in Brierley.
unit: Odette grew up in Brierley as part of a close circle of four friends alongside Nell Harcourt. She joined the Regent's class to qualify as a teacher and began her career instructing pupils at Stonebridge. Later in her youth, her brother Barney persuaded her to convey a proposal of marriage to Nell on his behalf, though Nell rejected the offer. Following a return from the West, Odette became engaged to Mr. Inglis, a wealthy former English miner from Winnipeg. In late May, she married Mr. Inglis and moved with him to live in luxury, traveling to Europe and establishing a home in Winnipeg. Despite her elevated wealth, she remained unpretentious, friendly, and close to her old friends, returning to share enthusiastically in Nell's wedding preparations.

Later in her youth, her brother Barney persuaded her to convey a proposal of marriage to Nell on his behalf, though Nell rejected the offer. Following a return from the West, Odette became engaged to Mr. Inglis, a wealthy former English miner from Winnipeg. In late May, she married Mr. Inglis and moved with him to live in luxury, traveling to Europe and establishing a home in Winnipeg. Despite her elevated wealth, she remained unpretentious, friendly, and close to her old friends, returning to share enthusiastically in Nell's wedding preparations.

label: Quotes
value: > Floating downward does not bother me when two or three of us are occupying the flat and we are able to sit upright. During those times, it is enjoyable. However, lying flat and acting as if I were deceased—that is something I simply could not do. Fear would actually kill me.

label: Quotes
value: > The cemetery appears so peculiar under the moon’s light! So spectral! Nell, the time is drawing near when I will be resting in that place. You, Isolde, and everyone else will be moving around, brimming with vitality—while I will be situated there—within the ancient cemetery—deceased!

label: Quotes
value: > Because—because—oh, Nell, I am not scared that I will fail to get into heaven. I belong to the church. But—everything there is going to be so unfamiliar. I ponder—and ponder—and it makes me so scared—and—and—homesick. Of course, heaven has to be extremely beautiful, as the Bible states—however, Nell, it will not be like what I am accustomed to.

value: Opal was widely considered the most beautiful girl in her school and community.
unit: Opal was widely considered the most beautiful girl in her school and community, possessing striking features, a radiant complexion, big vivid blue eyes, and a full, eye-catching figure. During her fatal illness, her complexion grew pale with a hectic flush and she appeared thin and childlike. In death, her features were so hallowed and delicate that she was remembered as the most beautiful deceased person seen in Brierley.

label: History
value: Opal grew up in Brierley.
unit: Opal grew up in Brierley as one of several daughters in the Pettigrew family. As a young student, she participated in local games, such as an attempt to dramatize Tennyson's Arthurian poetry at Pembroke's pond, though she declined to play Elaine due to her fear of acting deceased. While attending Regent's Academy, she was recognized as the most beautiful girl in her class and frequently walked home from the train accompanied by Hugh Carrow. She later took up a position as a teacher at Pale Sands school. However, her health began to fail rapidly, forcing her to step down until the new year. Throughout her final summer, she suffered from a consuming illness—likely consumption—and spent many smoky afternoons in her family's garden resting in a hammock. Realizing her approaching end, she confided her terror of death and the unfamiliarity of heaven to Nell Harcourt. She passed away peacefully in her sleep the morning after a village party, leaving an unfinished piece of needlework to Nell. She was laid to rest in the ancient cemetery near the Brierley church.

label: History
value: Mr. Pettifer purchased Robert Bell's farm
unit: After purchasing Robert Bell's farm in Brierley, Mr. Pettifer quickly developed a reputation for eccentricity, living alone without women and maintaining irregular dining and dishwashing habits. He hired John Henry Carter of Pale Sands as a farmhand and later employed another clumsy worker. When Nell Harcourt mistakenly sold his Jersey cow after finding it in her field, she visited his home to confess. Though initially quick-tempered, he treated Nell gently and hosted her for tea, leading the two to form a friendly relationship. Nell later confided in him about her ambition to write a story, though he gave her little encouragement, remarking that too much rubbish was already published.

label: History
value: Mr. Pidgeon is the schoolmaster of Brierley School.
unit: As the schoolmaster of Brierley School, Mr. Pidgeon tutored older pupils in preparation for Regent's examinations, including instructing students in subjects like geometry and algebra. During a school day, he miswrote Nell Harcourt's name without the final 'e' on the blackboard, prompting Hugh Carrow to tease her and leading to a classroom disturbance where Nell smashed her slate over Hugh's head; Mr. Pidgeon punished Nell by forcing her to stand on the dais while writing a public admonition about her temper on the board. On a subsequent day, after attempting to enforce strict arrival times following dinner, he singled out Nell when she ran into the schoolhouse alongside the tardy boys and forced her to sit next to Hugh Carrow as a sarcastic penalty. His harsh treatment and mockery caused Nell to refuse to return to school, prompting her to study at home instead.

label: History
value: Ezra Hale studied theology at St. Columbia
unit: Ezra Hale studied theology at St. Columbia and took charge of the Point Prospect Mission Church over a summer. While at Prospect Point, he befriended Cressida (Cressy), taking her boating, fishing, and strolling along the shore, while also delivering a powerful sermon at the village church that deeply moved her. Although initially reluctant to join the ministry, he embraced it as his divine purpose. He gave Cressy a rule of thumb for making choices—to act as she would wish to have acted when eighty years old—and comfortably accepted her lighthearted nature. By the following spring, he finished his studies at St. Columbia and made plans to take over a small slum mission church on Tanner Street, with he and Cressy set to be married a year from the coming June.

After his father Richard Farrow passed away from consumption, Robin and Lucy were left a trust fund, ensuring Grey Shutters would remain their permanent home. Upon starting school, he became close friends with classmate Milty Gammon and declared himself betrothed to Mabel Fletcher. He also grew two inches in height over a year and sold one of his lost teeth to Milty for two cents. Robin remains deeply attached to Nell, often seeking her reassurance, confessing his misdeeds to her, and listening eagerly to her explanations and fairytales.

label: History
value: Rosalind Penrose grew up as the daughter of old Mr. Penrose
unit: Rosalind Penrose grew up as the daughter of old Mr. Penrose, who built an ancient sandstone house bounded by an overgrown dyke and spruces. In her youth, she was considered a beauty and became engaged to Stephen Stanhope, but their betrothal broke off following a disagreement twenty-five years prior, leading him to move to the States. Over time, she withdrew from social life and lived quietly in her stone dwelling with her handmaiden, Belinda the Fourth. When Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke lost their way in the woods, Rosalind invited them in to share tea that she had originally prepared for an imagined gathering. During their visit, Nell mentioned Cedric Stanhope, prompting Rosalind to inquire quietly if he was Stephen's son before parting with gifts of lavender. She later hosted Nell and Cedric for another tea at her stone home.

In her youth, she was considered a beauty and became engaged to Stephen Stanhope, but their betrothal broke off following a disagreement twenty-five years prior, leading him to move to the States. Over time, she withdrew from social life and lived quietly in her stone dwelling with her handmaiden, Belinda the Fourth. When Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke lost their way in the woods, Rosalind invited them in to share tea that she had originally prepared for an imagined gathering. During their visit, Nell mentioned Cedric Stanhope, prompting Rosalind to inquire quietly if he was Stephen's son before parting with gifts of lavender. She later hosted Nell and Cedric for another tea at her stone home.

value: Eighteen years prior, Rufus visited Uncle Abner.
unit: Eighteen years prior, at around seventeen years of age, Rufus visited his Uncle Abner. He sowed crops at the farm before departing on the vessel Four Sisters for Havana, Cuba. Upon reaching Cuba, Rufus contracted yellow fever. His double cousin, Laurence Vane, remained behind in Cuba to care for him while the vessel departed. Rufus died of the disease shortly thereafter. For eleven years, the community of Seven Gulls mistakenly believed that Laurence Vane—who had survived a violent injury with severe memory loss and a altered appearance—was Rufus Vane returned home.

label: History
value: Rupert Ashdown is a child.
unit: Rupert Ashdown is one of the minister's children residing at the manse in Fern Hollow. On a dare from local boys, he threw Link Drew's large eel—which he mistakenly believed was dead—into old Mrs. Carr's carriage, causing her to leap out when the eel revived. The incident sparked public outrage, leading his father, Reverend Ashdown, to decide to whip him. Though Rupert accepted the punishment bravely to avoid distressing his father further, Mr. Ashdown ultimately could not bring himself to lash his son upon seeing Cecelia's eyes in him. To punish himself for a lack of courage during a previous ghost scare, Rupert enforced a midnight vigil atop Mr. Pollock's tombstone in the cemetery. During a soaking cold drizzle, he remained on the gravestone until midnight out of honor. Consequently, he contracted double pneumonia and became dangerously ill, bringing severe alarm to his father and siblings. Dr. Hugh Carrow and a nurse stayed by his bedside to fight the fever until he finally recovered, after which local church members showered the manse with provisions to celebrate his health.

label: History
value: Tabitha entered service at Hollowmere.
unit: Tabitha entered service as a gray, austere servant at Hollowmere for the Carrow household. When Nell fell gravely ill after giving birth to her infant son Harcourt, Tabitha took complete charge of caring for the baby, forming an intense maternal affection for him that led her to shield him fiercely from any physical discipline. During a three-month period when Dr. Carrow and Nell traveled to London, Tabitha cared for Harcourt at her brother's home while the other children went to Brierley. When Nell went into labor at the house of dreams, Tabitha helped manage the home and offered fierce comfort during the uncertain ordeal. On another occasion when the Ashdown children fled in terror from a supposed phantom, Tabitha marched out into Fern Hollow armed with a pitchfork to investigate, uncovering that the ghost was merely old Mrs. Stimson retrieving bleached cotton sheets from an embankment.

When Nell fell gravely ill after giving birth to her infant son Harcourt, Tabitha took complete charge of caring for the baby, forming an intense maternal affection for him that led her to shield him fiercely from any physical discipline. During a three-month period when Dr. Carrow and Nell traveled to London, Tabitha cared for Harcourt at her brother's home while the other children went to Brierley. When Nell went into labor at the house of dreams, Tabitha helped manage the home and offered fierce comfort during the uncertain ordeal. On another occasion when the Ashdown children fled in terror from a supposed phantom, Tabitha marched out into Fern Hollow armed with a pitchfork to investigate, uncovering that the ghost was merely old Mrs. Stimson retrieving bleached cotton sheets from an embankment.

label: History
value: Tessa was entrusted by Tabitha with a delicate task.
unit: Tessa was entrusted by Tabitha with a delicate task: bringing a small basket of carefully cultivated early strawberries from Hollowmere to the Glen St. Agnes manse, with strict instructions to hand them over to no one other than Aunt Martha or Mr. Ashdown. Wearing her finest frock and an ornate hat, Tessa marched proudly up the manse hill to execute her errand. Upon reaching the lawn gate, she was confronted by Mary Stubbs, who attempted to seize the basket. Tessa resisted and refused to relinquish it, insisting on following her instructions. In retaliation, Mary performed an unsettling dance, made strange facial expressions, and eventually grabbed a large, dried codfish to chase her. Terrified by the bizarre weapon, Tessa dropped the basket, crushing the strawberries as she fled down the main street. During the pursuit, Tessa tripped and fell into a mud puddle at the end of the street, destroying her hat, dress, and slippers while bruising her pride. Miss Winifred rescued the crying child from the street and carried her home to be cleaned and comforted by Tabitha.

label: History
value: Thirza and Obed decided to adopt an orphan boy.
unit: Thirza and her brother Obed decided to adopt a ten or eleven-year-old orphan boy from Nova Scotia. Due to a mix-up in communication involving Nancy and Mrs. Tranter, an orphaned girl named Nell Harcourt was brought to Grey Shutters instead. Although Thirza initially planned to return Nell to the orphanage or hand her over to Mrs. Peter Scobie, she ultimately yielded to Obed's wishes and agreed to keep her. She taught Nell household duties and stood up for the child when Mrs. Agatha Sowerby insulted her appearance. Years later, Thirza also agreed to take in the orphaned twins Robin and Lucy Farrow at Grey Shutters, managing the farm's rental income to support the household and held funds in trust for their care after their father Richard Farrow died.

label: History
value: Miss Thorne served as a rural schoolteacher
unit: Miss Thorne served as a rural schoolteacher at Brierley School. During her tenure, she introduced Friday afternoon recitations, field trips to examine local flora and fauna, and daily physical culture routines. At the end of June, her term and reign at Brierley came to a close, leaving her students—including Nell and Isolde—deeply moved and tearful during her parting remarks. Prior to the Academy entrance examinations, she advised her pupils against last-minute studying, recommending instead that they take walks and rest early. She also personally accompanied several students, including Nell, Odette, Opal, and Flossie, to the Academy in town on their exam day.
